settlement_mentioned: homes built in unsafe areas too close to the Mthatha River; rural villages
P5_ev: Flooding has become more common and severe in South Africa as the impacts of climate change are felt.
P5_note: Also DM 18 Jun (Conradie): "rainfall from the cut-off low weather system along the east coast was probably becoming more intense due to climate change."
P2_ev: But a significant challenge is the availability of suitable land, as many of the destroyed homes were built in unsafe areas too close to the Mthatha River, where rebuilding is not an option.
P2_note: DM 19 Jun analysis also: 'Vulnerable populations are often pushed into these high-risk zones because of their proximity to employment' and 'unchecked development in flood-prone areas continues despite known risks'. Framing is unsafe-siting near river (rural/peri-urban), informal settlements mentioned generally.
P3_ev: President Cyril Ramaphosa has arrived in Mthatha. Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs (COGTA) Minister Velenkosini Hlabisa and Premier Oscar Mabuyane will accompany Ramaphosa as he visits the affected families.
